title: Condition Drift and Regrade Candidates
dataSources: Collection items (`collection:item`), intake scans (`collection:scan`), market prices (`collection:price`), item photos (`collection:photo`), authentication records (`collection:auth`), loans (`collection:loan`), and condition audits (`collection:condition`).
app: Collection telemetry from personal catalogues, NFC scans, pricing feeds, authentication records, loan logs, shelf measurements, and item-condition audits streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=collection:condition
| stats earliest(condition_score) as start_condition latest(condition_score) as current_condition by item_id title
| eval drop=current_condition-start_condition
| where drop<0
| sort drop
description: Finds items whose condition score has worsened enough that storage, handling, or regrading should be reviewed.
value: Condition drift is often subtle until it matters financially, so this keeps preservation issues from slipping by unnoticed.
implementation: Log condition audits for higher-value items with a consistent scoring approach and compare the newest score with the oldest one on file.
visualization: Table of items with negative condition drift.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which items seem to be getting worn or damaged over time and may need extra care.
